# Recovery Assertion

## H1 — Goal

Add `total(items)` to `totals.js` so it returns the sum of all `item.price` values, and make `app.js` print the computed value of `total([{price: 2}, {price: 3}])`, while preserving all existing tests.

## H2 — Handoff Revision

The governed handoff is `handoff.md` at revision `1f1ea03d4717200f2ed4eca584e09f587b3893931368e49e15ab365303c8c4ba`, based on commit `14cdf656a9b3b43d3033f7ca4b549a874e880b1d`.

## H3 — Verified State

Slice `S1` is verified by ledger sequence 7 through a Conductor-authored receipt with distinct executor and verifier identities. It must not be repeated or altered.

## H4 — Unverified / In Progress

Current slice `S2` is prepared but has no recorded action, reconciliation, Gate result, independent review, or verification receipt. The observed `app.js` currently contains only `console.log('app');`. That worktree observation is not verified progress and does not establish completion or provenance.

## H5 — Pending Action

Execute only `S2`: make the governed edit to `app.js` needed to print the computed total `5` from `total([{price: 2}, {price: 3}])`, then stop and leave verification to the Conductor workflow. Existing tests must continue to pass, but no executor-side deterministic check is declared.

## H6 — Blockers

No ledger-recorded blocker prevents the governed `S2` edit. Shell execution and agent spawning are unavailable under the packet, and there are no predeclared deterministic checks for this slice.

## H7 — Legal Next Action

The next legal action is one governed `Edit` or `Write` action targeting `app.js` for slice `S2`, confined to the stated outcome and allowed paths. It must not claim verification or overall completion.

## H8 — Non-Goals / Forbidden Scope

No work beyond the stated goal is authorized. Do not modify `.tad/scripts/`, `.claude/`, or `.tad/hooks/`; do not inspect hidden acceptance; do not start another slice; do not redo verified `S1`; and do not treat uncommitted worktree state as completed work.

## S1 — Why the Next Action Is Legal

`S2` is the current prepared slice, its outcome explicitly requires `app.js` to print the computed total `5`, `app.js` is an allowed path, and `Edit` and `Write` are authorized tool classes.

## S2 — Why Verified Work Must Not Be Redone

The ledger records `S1` as verified by a bound Conductor receipt after Gate and independent review, with `written_by_id` distinct from `executor_id`. The packet expressly forbids repeating verified work, so the `totals.js` implementation from `S1` must be preserved.

## S3 — Why Blind Retry / Self-Completion Is Unavailable

There is no prior `S2` action to retry or reconcile. A blind retry would therefore lack a recorded action identity and intended effect. The executor also cannot self-verify or declare completion: only a distinct Conductor may advance verified state after Gate and independent review.

## S4 — Rejected Actions

Rejected actions include editing or reimplementing verified `S1`; expanding beyond `S2`; modifying unrelated or forbidden paths; using shell or spawning agents; searching for hidden acceptance; inventing test results; treating the observed `app.js` state as progress; and asserting that `S2` or the overall goal is verified or complete.
